steps.text: Write the introduction for a working paper on Modal Transition Systems that proposes a restricted subclass with its own notion of refinement. Cover background on MTS and refinement, the incompleteness problem the work responds to, the key idea of the new subclass, a list of contributions, and a short overview of the paper's sections.

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Background
  - MTS (cite) extend LTS (cite): two kinds of transitions, necessary (must) vs optional (may) behaviour in a spec
  - refinement = design step: some optional behaviour discarded, other optional becomes necessary
  - stepwise refinement -> implementation = LTS, no further refinement possible
  - critical for formal reasoning on correctness of design/implementation: abstract spec -> concrete, each step correct
  - well-known specification theory, significant advances (cite)
- Problem
  - modal refinement not complete (cite)
  - two MTS not in refinement relation although implementation sets included (= thorough refinement)
  - MTS refinement polynomial time; thorough refinement EXPTIME (cite)
  - prior work (cite) leaves open: alternative modal refinement sound and complete wrt implementations
  - also need: set of implementations interesting in practice (no valuable implementation disregarded)
- Proposal
  - working paper; subset of MTS: NMTS, alternative modal refinement \preceq_{n}
  - insight: states non-deterministically reachable by identical action sequences are related
  - outgoing transitions with same action label share same modality
  - refinement deactivating one optional transition deactivates all same-label transitions from related (source) states
- Contributions
  - 1. NMTS subset: same label + reachable by same sequence -> same modality
  - 2. NMTS refinement: from modal refinement + extra constraint on optional transitions of system being refined
  - 3. examples of MTS failing to be NMTS or NMTS refinements
  - 4. non-reducible non-determinism property for optional non-deterministic actions; inherent, preserved in any implementation where action stays active; implementations accepted by MTS refinement but discarded by NMTS refinement violate it
  - 5. example (Figure 7): NMTS refinement not transitive; two systems in NMTS refinement though implementations not in set inclusion
## Overview
  - Sec 2 background MTS + modal refinement; Sec 3 NMTS + refinement; Sec 4 non-reducible non-determinism, discarded implementations violate it; Sec 5 related work; Sec 6 conclusions + future work

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Modal Transition Systems (MTS) are an extension of Labelled Transition Systems (LTS). They distinguish two types of transitions, which describe necessary and optional behaviour in a system specification: transitions that must necessarily be implemented and transitions that may optionally be implemented. MTS have a concept of refinement, which represents a step of the design process, namely the step where some optional behaviour is discarded and some other optional behaviour becomes necessary. If you refine an MTS step by step you eventually get an implementation, which is an LTS where no more refinement is possible. Refinement of MTS is critical for formal reasoning on the correctness of the design and implementation of a system, because it lets you gradually refine an abstract specification into a concrete one and make sure each step is correct. MTS are a well-known specification theory and there have been significant advances so far.

It is known that the (modal) refinement of MTS is not complete. This means that there are cases where two MTS are not in a refinement relation even though the set of implementations of one MTS is included in the set of implementations of the other MTS (this relation is called thorough refinement). Also, MTS refinement can be computed in polynomial time, but determining thorough refinement of MTS requires EXPTIME. In prior work, the problem of finding an alternative notion of modal refinement that is both sound and complete with respect to its set of implementations is left open. It is also important to show that the set of implementations considered is interesting from a practical point of view too (i.e., no valuable implementation is thrown away).

- Proposal: NMTS, subset of MTS, refinement \preceq_{n}; states reachable non-deterministically by identical action sequences are related; same label -> same modality; deactivating one optional transition deactivates same-label transitions from related (source) states
- Contributions 1-5: NMTS definition; NMTS refinement (extra constraint on optional transitions); counterexamples; non-reducible non-determinism property (discarded implementations violate it); Figure 7 example, not transitive, no set inclusion
## Overview
- Sec 2 background; Sec 3 NMTS; Sec 4 non-reducible non-determinism; Sec 5 related work; Sec 6 conclusions/future work

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Modal Transition Systems (MTS) are an extension of Labelled Transition Systems (LTS). They distinguish two types of transitions, which describe necessary and optional behaviour in a system specification: transitions that must necessarily be implemented and transitions that may optionally be implemented. MTS have a concept of refinement, which represents a step of the design process, namely the step where some optional behaviour is discarded and some other optional behaviour becomes necessary. If you refine an MTS step by step you eventually get an implementation, which is an LTS where no more refinement is possible. Refinement of MTS is critical for formal reasoning on the correctness of the design and implementation of a system, because it lets you gradually refine an abstract specification into a concrete one and make sure each step is correct. MTS are a well-known specification theory and there have been significant advances so far.

It is known that the (modal) refinement of MTS is not complete. This means that there are cases where two MTS are not in a refinement relation even though the set of implementations of one MTS is included in the set of implementations of the other MTS (this relation is called thorough refinement). Also, MTS refinement can be computed in polynomial time, but determining thorough refinement of MTS requires EXPTIME. In prior work, the problem of finding an alternative notion of modal refinement that is both sound and complete with respect to its set of implementations is left open. It is also important to show that the set of implementations considered is interesting from a practical point of view too (i.e., no valuable implementation is thrown away).

In this working paper we propose a subset of MTS, called Non-reducible Modal Transition Systems (NMTS), together with an alternative notion of modal refinement \preceq_{n}. The basic insight behind NMTS is that states that are reachable non-deterministically by executing identical sequences of actions are related. In particular, the outgoing transitions that share the same action label also share the same modality. Also, when a refinement step deactivates one optional transition, this deactivates all the other transitions with the same label from all the other related (source) states.

The contributions of the paper are:

- 1. we introduce NMTS, which are a subset of MTS. In NMTS, transitions that share the same action label must also share the same modality when they are reachable by the same sequence of actions;

- 2. we give NMTS an alternative notion of modal refinement, which we call NMTS refinement. NMTS refinement comes from modal refinement with an additional constraint on the optional transitions of the system that is refined;

- 3. we give different examples of MTS that do not meet the requisites for being NMTS or refinements of NMTS;

- 4. we introduce the non-reducible non-determinism property about optional, non-deterministic actions. This non-determinism is inherent in these actions and should be kept in any implementation where the action is still active. All the implementations that the standard MTS refinement accepts but the NMTS refinement discards are shown to violate the non-reducible non-determinism property.

- 5. we give an example (Figure 7) showing that NMTS refinement is not transitive, and where two systems are in NMTS refinement even though their implementations are not in a relation of set inclusion.

## Overview

Section 2 gives background on MTS and modal refinement. Section 3 presents Non-reducible MTS (NMTS) and their refinement. Section 4 discusses the non-reducible non-determinism property and shows that the implementations discarded by NMTS refinement but accepted by modal refinement violate it. Section 5 is about related work, and Section 6 concludes the paper and discusses future work.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Modal Transition Systems (MTS) [1] extend Labelled Transition Systems (LTS) [2] by distinguishing two types of transitions, meant to describe necessary and optional behaviour in a system specification: transitions that must necessarily be implemented and transitions that may optionally be implemented. MTS come with a concept of refinement, which represents a step of the design process, namely the one in which some optional behaviour is discarded while other optional behaviour becomes necessary. Stepwise refinement of an MTS eventually results in an implementation, which is an LTS in which no further refinement is possible. Refinement of MTS is critical for formal reasoning on the correctness of a system's design and implementation, since it enables gradually refining an abstract specification into a concrete one while ensuring that each step is correct. MTS are a well-known specification theory and significant advances have been made so far [3,4].

It is known that the (modal) refinement of MTS is not complete (cf., e.g., [5]). In other words, there are cases in which two MTS are not in a refinement relation although the set of implementations of one MTS is included in the set of implementations of the other (this relation is known as thorough refinement). Furthermore, while MTS refinement can be computed in polynomial time, determining thorough refinement of MTS requires EXPTIME [6]. In [5], the problem of proposing an alternative notion of modal refinement that is both sound and complete with respect to its set of implementations is left open. It is also essential to demonstrate that the considered set of implementations is interesting from a practical point of view (i.e., no valuable implementation is disregarded).

In this working paper, we propose a subset of MTS, called Non-reducible Modal Transition Systems (NMTS), together with their alternative notion of modal refinement \preceq_{n}. A fundamental insight behind NMTS is that states non-deterministically reachable through the execution of identical sequences of actions are related. Specifically, outgoing transitions sharing the same action label also share the same modality. Furthermore, when a refinement step deactivates one optional transition, this deactivates all other transitions sharing the same label from all other related (source) states.

The contributions of this paper are:

- 1. we introduce NMTS, a subset of MTS, in which transitions sharing the same action label are constrained to also share the same modality whenever they are reachable by the same sequence of actions;

- 2. we equip NMTS with an alternative notion of modal refinement, called NMTS refinement, derived from modal refinement by imposing an additional constraint on the optional transitions of the system to be refined;

- 3. we provide different examples of MTS instances that fail to meet the requisites for being either NMTS or refinements of NMTS;

- 4. we introduce the non-reducible non-determinism property concerning optional, non-deterministic actions. This non-determinism is inherent in such actions and should be preserved in any implementation where the action remains active. All implementations accepted by the standard MTS refinement but discarded by the NMTS refinement are shown to violate the non-reducible non-determinism property.

- 5. we provide an example (Figure 7) demonstrating that NMTS refinement is not transitive, in which two systems are in NMTS refinement although their implementations are not in a relation of set inclusion.

## Overview

Section 2 introduces background on MTS and modal refinement. Section 3 presents Non-reducible MTS (NMTS) and their refinement. Section 4 discusses the non-reducible non-determinism property, showing that the implementations discarded by NMTS refinement but accepted by modal refinement violate it. Section 5 discusses related work, and Section 6 concludes the paper and discusses future work.
